scenes.title: The Original Grid and Basis Vectors
scenes.visual: A 2D Cartesian coordinate plane with light blue grid lines spanning from -4 to 4 on both axes. Two bold arrows start at the origin: a green arrow i-hat pointing right to (1,0) with label 'i-hat = [1, 0]' in green text at the top left, and a red arrow j-hat pointing up to (0,1) with label 'j-hat = [0, 1]' below it.
scenes.narration: A linear transformation is a way of altering space while keeping lines straight and the origin fixed. Everything in 2D space is anchored by two fundamental unit vectors: i-hat and j-hat.

scenes.title: Transforming the Grid
scenes.visual: The coordinate grid smoothly skews and rotates over 3 seconds. The original grid fades to background grey while a new yellow grid deforms to show the transformed plane. The green vector moves smoothly from (1,0) to (2,1), and the red vector moves smoothly from (0,1) to (-1,2).
scenes.narration: When a matrix acts on the plane, the entire grid transforms with it. Notice how grid lines remain parallel and evenly spaced, but their orientation and scale change.

scenes.title: Matrix as Destination of Basis Vectors
scenes.visual: The transformed plane remains visible in the background. A 2x2 matrix equation appears in a white background box at the top right: column 1 shows [2, 1] in green, column 2 shows [-1, 2] in red. An arrow points from the green transformed vector to the first column of the matrix, and another arrow points from the red vector to the second column.
scenes.narration: To describe the entire transformation, we only need to track where i-hat and j-hat land. The columns of a matrix are simply the new coordinates of these two basis vectors.
